blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: The book explicitly attributes a harmful spirit affecting Saul to the LORD after the Spirit of the LORD departs; medical, psychological, spiritual, and theological explanations should not be collapsed into one diagnosis. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

A literary feature to notice is that The David and Goliath account exists in a substantially shorter ancient Greek form and a longer Masoretic form; reconstruction of their literary relationship remains disputed. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. Interpretations differ on some details.
